data.long_meaning: The name Sharvikaarna is derived from two Sanskrit words - Sharvi and Karna. Sharvi is a name of the goddess Saraswati, who is the goddess of knowledge, music, arts, wisdom, and learning. Karna means 'powerful'. Thus, Sharvikaarna means 'Goddess Sharvi, the Powerful'. The name Sharvikaarna carries the meaning “Goddess Sharvi + Powerful” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sharvikaarna usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess sharvi + powerful and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: This name signifies the divine grace and blessings of the goddess Saraswati, who bestows wisdom, knowledge, and creativity upon her devotees. It also represents the inner strength and power of the individual.
data.etymology: Sharvikaarna belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess Sharvi + Powerful.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sharvikaarna total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

Saraswati, the goddess of wisdom, knowledge, and arts, is revered not just in Hinduism but also in Jainism, Buddhism, and Sikhism. The name Sharvikaarna is a reminder of the great importance of learning and wisdom in Hindu culture. It also signifies the power and strength associated with the Goddess Sharvi.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sharvikaarna also holds great spiritual significance. The name Sharvi relates to Saraswati, who represents the purity of thought and the power of wisdom. Karna, on the other hand, signifies power and strength. Thus, the name Sharvikaarna represents the combination of purity of thought, power of wisdom, and the strength to use that wisdom in the righteous way.
